description: Group D - Observability. D1 session trace / replay export: auto-capture a per-step record (screenshot + snapshot + decision + confidence + timing) during a run and expose a NEW tool laya_export_run that writes an HTML and/or JSON replay artifact to a path (building on the existing Playwright tracing). D2 structured MCP progress notifications: stream step progress over the MCP protocol (notifications/progress) so the CLIENT UI shows 'step 3/15: clicking Sign in', using the SDK progress mechanism. Depends on FEAT-002 (loop step records) and FEAT-003 (redaction must apply to exported/streamed text too). Registered under an appropriate capability; keep additive.
steps: D1 per-step recording: extend the loop to accumulate a per-step observability record while it runs: for each step capture step number, operation, target, confidences, source, detail (already redacted per B1), timing (ms for the step), and a screenshot (page.screenshot({type:'png'}) as a base64/Buffer) plus the compact snapshot text. Store these on the RunResult via a NEW optional field `steps?: RunStepArtifact[]` (additive; do not change existing transcript/StepRecord). Keep screenshots optional/bounded (only capture when export/recording is enabled to avoid slowing normal runs) - add RunGoalOptions.recordArtifacts?: boolean (default false) and enable it when the export tool or a config flag requests it. Because the server holds one session, keep the most recent run's artifacts accessible (e.g. store lastRunArtifacts on a small holder passed to run_goal + export tools, or on the session). Redaction from B1 must apply to any text in the artifacts.

D1 export tool: create src/tools/export_run.ts implementing laya_export_run with inputSchema { path: string (output file or directory), format?: 'html'|'json'|'both' (default 'both') }. It writes a JSON replay (steps with decision/confidence/timing/snapshot + embedded base64 screenshots) and/or a self-contained HTML replay page (inline the screenshots + a per-step list) to the given path, returning the written path(s) and byte sizes. Reuse Node fs/promises for writing (no stdout). If no run has been recorded yet, return a clear text result saying to run laya_run_goal first. Register it in src/tools/index.ts REGISTRY under the 'devtools' capability (alongside tracing) and add it to registry wiring; document it in the README Tools -> DEVTOOLS table and the divergence/notes as appropriate. Ensure it complements (does not replace) browser_start_tracing/browser_stop_tracing.

D2 progress notifications: in src/tools/run_goal.ts makeHandler, accept the MCP handler's second `extra` argument (RequestHandlerExtra) and, when extra._meta.progressToken is present, send a notifications/progress for each step via extra.sendNotification({ method: 'notifications/progress', params: { progressToken, progress, total, message } }) where progress=step, total=maxSteps, and message like 'step 3/15: clicking Sign in' (redacted). Wire this by passing an onProgress callback into runGoal via RunGoalOptions.onProgress?: (info:{step:number,total:number,message:string})=>void|Promise<void>; the loop calls it at the same place it calls narrator.progress(step,max) (and when it sets the acting caption) so the client UI mirrors the on-page overlay. Keep it a no-op when no progressToken/onProgress is provided so existing behavior is unchanged. Make the run_goal handler signature compatible with the SDK ToolCallback (args, extra).

Update README: add laya_export_run to the DEVTOOLS tools table with a description; add a short Observability subsection under Autopilot (or How it works) describing the per-step replay export and the MCP progress-notification streaming (step N/max), and note the redaction applies to exported/streamed text.

Add tests. test/export-run.test.ts (real headless chromium): run a goal with recordArtifacts enabled, call laya_export_run to a temp path with format 'both', and assert both the JSON and HTML files are written and NON-EMPTY, the JSON parses and contains per-step decision/confidence/timing entries, and any secret text is masked. test/progress-notifications.test.ts: invoke the run_goal handler with a fake `extra` that has _meta.progressToken set and a captured sendNotification sink; assert at least one notifications/progress with the progressToken, a numeric progress/total, and a 'step N/' message was emitted; and assert NO notifications are emitted when no progressToken is present (backward-compat).
acceptance_criteria: RunResult gains only an OPTIONAL `steps?` artifacts field; existing transcript/StepRecord/verification/outcome fields are unchanged.

laya_export_run writes a non-empty JSON and/or HTML replay artifact to the given path (format both by default), the JSON parses and contains per-step decision + confidence + timing, and secret text is masked; it is registered under the devtools capability and documented.

When the caller supplies a progressToken, the run_goal handler emits notifications/progress per step (with progressToken, numeric progress/total, and a 'step N/max: ...' message); when no progressToken is supplied, no progress notifications are emitted and behavior is unchanged.
Artifact recording is off by default (recordArtifacts=false) so normal runs are not slowed; the export tool enables it.
verification: Run `npx vitest run test/export-run.test.ts test/progress-notifications.test.ts` and confirm D1/D2 assertions pass headless.
Run `npm run test` and `npm run typecheck` and confirm the full suite passes with the 3 pre-existing skips intact.
Run `npm run build` and confirm dist/ emits cleanly (the new tool + handler compile).
